text:
alex: Heads-up — ran a seq_len sweep across A100 / H100 / L40S comparing paged, fused-flash and classic flash variants. Weird regression on H100: 12-18% slower at seq=4096 when KV cache is warm vs cold. attaching short logs below. anyone seen this? :thinking:

maria: Can you paste the exact bench command + runtime build + model config?

alex: Sure — repro command and commit: 
```
./tools/run_attention_bench.sh --model gpt2-xl --kernels paged,fused_flash,flash_classic \ 
  --gpus a100,h100,l40s --bsz 1,4,8 --seq 512,1024,2048,4096 \ 
  --prefetch on --kv_eviction lru --batcher continuous --soft_delay_ms 2 \ 
  --commit abc123def
```
Summary (throughput tokens/s, H100 shows the anomaly):
```
A100  seq=4096 bsz=1 fused_flash  85k t/s
H100  seq=4096 bsz=1 fused_flash  70k t/s  <-- 18% drop vs cold
L40S  seq=4096 bsz=1 fused_flash  62k t/s
H100 (cold-cache) seq=4096 bsz=1 fused_flash  84k t/s
```

taylor: Huh. We saw kv-prefetch + eviction thrash on L40S in a different test. Did you enable prefetch? what eviction policy? :eyes:

alex: prefetch=on, kv_eviction=LRU, batcher=continuous, soft_delay=2ms. Config snippet: 
```
{"prefetch":"on","kv_eviction":"lru","batcher":"continuous","soft_delay_ms":2}
```

josh: Any flamegraph / profiler output? sounds like memcpy or kernel-launch latency blowups.

alex: Pulled a quick perf trace (nvprof/cupti sampling). Top lines: memcpy and kernel launch overhead spike on H100 when kv_hits high. Excerpt: 
```
[profiler] memcpy H2D: 42%  (was 18% cold)
[profiler] kernel_launch_overhead: 24% (was 8% cold)
[kernel_selector] chosen: seq<=1024 -> fused_flash_v2, seq>=2048 -> paged_flash_v1
```
So kernel_selector flips to paged_flash for long sequences; with KV warm the memory layout/IO pattern changes and we pay scatter memcpy + more launches.

maria: Try two quick experiments: 1) disable prefetch on H100, 2) bump soft_delay_ms to 10 to let the batcher coalesce a bit. If perf recovers it's likely a batching/prefetch interaction.

alex: Ran both. Results: disabling prefetch recovers ~14% (close to cold). soft_delay_ms=10 gives +8% (partial). So prefetch looks like main vector. Repro logs show: 
```
[kv_cache] warm=true hit_rate=0.94 size=1.2GB
[prefetch] scheduled_prefetches=128 -> many small copies
[kernel_selector] chose paged_flash_v1 for seq=4096 even though fused_flash gave better end-to-end for warm-kv
```

taylor: That indicates our selector threshold is based on seq only, not kv_hit_rate or contiguous-kv-layout. On H100 the scatter memcpy cost dominates. We should feed in a metric like kv_hit_density or prefetch_write_bytes to selector.

perf-bot: Benchmark run summary: run=1732109876, anomaly_flag=true, affected=H100(seq>=2048), metric=throughput_drop, severity=medium

eva: I'll open a bisect + kernel-selector ticket and try a quick patch: bias selector toward fused_flash when kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.8 AND seq > 2048 on H100. Assigning to eng-runtime. @alex can you attach full traces + raw nvprof files to the ticket? :thumbsup:

alex: Yep attaching traces to the ticket now. For immediate mitigation I'm going to disable prefetch for H100 in the runtime config and roll that tomorrow. Thanks all!
